title: Chalazion incision and curettage
subtitle: Clamp, vertical conjunctival incision, curettage and histology when atypical

sources.org: Ben Simon GJ et al. Am J Ophthalmol 151:714
sources.title: Intralesional triamcinolone acetonide injection versus incision and curettage for primary chalazia: a prospective, randomized study

indications: A chalazion persisting despite warm compresses and lid hygiene for several weeks.
A large chalazion causing astigmatism, ptosis or cosmetic concern.
contraindications: A recurrent chalazion in the same place, or one with atypical features, in an older adult: biopsy for sebaceous carcinoma rather than curette alone.
preparation: Check the lid for signs of malignancy (loss of lashes, ulceration, distortion of the lid margin, recurrence).
Consent: recurrence, bleeding and bruising, a visible lid notch rarely, and histology if indicated.
positioning: Supine or semi-reclined, head supported; children usually under general anaesthesia.
equipment: Chalazion clamp, 11 blade, small curette, fine scissors, local anaesthetic with adrenaline, topical anaesthetic, antibiotic ointment, eye pad.
anatomy: The tarsal plate with the meibomian glands running vertically within it, the conjunctival surface behind, the lid margin and lash line in front.
criticalSafety: Incise vertically on the conjunctival side, at least 2 to 3 mm from the lid margin.
Send tissue for histology when recurrent or atypical.
Protect the cornea from the clamp and instruments.
commonErrors: A horizontal incision that cuts across glands.
An incision too close to the lid margin.
Curetting a sebaceous carcinoma without histology.
postop: Pad for a few hours; antibiotic ointment for a few days.
Warm compresses and lid hygiene to prevent new chalazia.
Return if it recurs in the same place.

steps.emphasis: Mark the lid (upper or lower, right or left).
Topical drops, then local anaesthetic with adrenaline infiltrated subcutaneously and subconjunctivally around the lesion.
Send the contents and wall for histology if recurrent or atypical, and in older adults.
Remove the clamp and press firmly for several minutes.
Antibiotic ointment and a firm pad for a few hours.

step.chal.clamp.title: Applying the chalazion clamp
step.chal.clamp.why: The clamp everts the lid, controls bleeding and protects the cornea, so the incision can be made accurately on the conjunctival side.
how: Place the ring of the clamp on the conjunctival side around the lesion and the solid plate on the skin side.
Tighten it just enough to stop bleeding and evert the lid.
pitfalls: Clamp ring not centred on the lesion.

step.chal.incise.title: Vertical incision and curettage
step.chal.incise.why: A vertical incision follows the meibomian glands and spares the lid margin; thorough curettage and removal of the wall reduce recurrence.
how: Incise vertically through the conjunctiva and tarsus over the lesion, stopping 2 to 3 mm short of the lid margin.
Curette out the contents in all directions, and excise the wall with fine scissors.
Inspect the contents: unusual yellow, firm or gritty tissue raises the suspicion of carcinoma.
